answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil identities by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its votes earn influence. A newcomer must keep capital immobilized through a review window, while colluding identities that endorse the same fabricated work lose that stake when challenged with evidence. The reward is not worth multiplying accounts: every extra identity adds a real bond and exposure. A marble deposit, a whisper network, or a ripple of copied identities cannot make those costs disappear.
